To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The Nordic welfare states are undergoing a process of transformation, which is affecting the health risks that people face and the way they invest in their bodies.

(1) health risks have changed in the context of the welfare state; (2) the new risks are often diffuse, and hence hard to detect; (3) they are also often invisible, and hence not visible in the welfare state; and (4) they may be related to the body, and hence are often experienced as embodied risks.

(1) the health risks of the new social class are related to abundance and affluence, (2) these health risks are often self-inflicted and (3) these health risks have a diffuse and often invisible character, and are thus not easily detected by the health system or the welfare state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
health risks and personal investments in the body in the context of the changing welfare states in the Nordic countries.
the changing health risks and how they are related to changing welfare states.
the new health risks and the personal investments in the body that are related to them, in the context of changing welfare states.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have seen that the new social risks are related to new forms of health risks and that these are related to new personal investments in the body.
the new health risks have become a major concern in the Nordic welfare states, and that these health risks are related to a new kind of personal investments in the body.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the health risks of today are not just about the body, but about the body in relation to the world.
the new health risks and the personal investments in health and the body that are related to them are not only about individual lifestyle choices.
the new health risks and the new social risks of the 21st century are intertwined in complex ways.
